title: Edge Inference — Apple Neural Engine, Qualcomm Hexagon, WebGPU/WebLLM, Jetson

questions.question: The same model runs fast on a flagship laptop but crawls on a mid-range phone. What fundamentally limits it there?
options: The model's intelligence
The color scheme of the app
The number of app features
Memory bandwidth against the weight size
questions.explanation: Decode reads all weights per token, so bandwidth sets the ceiling. This lesson sizes edge models to the weakest target device.

questions.question: For a 4.7 GB model on the 60 GB/s Apple A18 row, what ceiling is approximately implied?
options: 60 tok/s
12.8 tok/s
4.7 tok/s
About 282 tok/s
questions.explanation: The reciprocal is 60/4.7, about 12.8 tokens/s; the observed A18 value is lower because the ceiling is theoretical.

questions.question: What memory property distinguishes the Apple M4/A18 Neural Engine path in the lesson?
options: It requires a cross-region KV transfer
It uses separate HBM and CPU memory pools
Unified memory avoids a CPU-to-NPU copy
It supports only GGUF files in a browser
questions.explanation: The Apple path uses unified memory, so CPU and ANE share the pool; native ANE deployment still uses Core ML conversion.

questions.question: Which weight format does the WebGPU/WebLLM target table recommend?
options: GGUF Q4 without conversion
NVFP4 weights with FP8 KV
BF16 only
Q4 MLC (q4f16_1)
questions.explanation: The table specifies Q4 MLC q4f16_1 and a compiled wasm path; GGUF is explicitly not the WebGPU artifact in this lesson.

questions.question: Which browser support gap is called out for 2026?
options: Firefox Android lagging
Chrome Android cannot use WebGPU at all
Safari iOS 26 has no WebGPU landing
WebLLM works only on desktop Firefox
questions.explanation: The lesson reports Chrome Android v121+ and Safari iOS 26 support, with Firefox Android still catching up and overall mobile coverage around 70–75%.

questions.question: Why does the lesson call edge decode memory-bandwidth-bound?
options: The model reads no weights during decode
Mobile DRAM is 30–50× slower
TOPS is always zero on mobile NPUs
Network RTT dominates even when the model is local
questions.explanation: The same Q4 weights must be read for each token; mobile DRAM is 50–90 GB/s versus roughly 2–3 TB/s HBM3, so bandwidth sets the ceiling.
